summary.text:
Let me design the FB.

States: WAIT_A, MOVE_AB, WAIT_B, MOVE_BC, WAIT_C, DONE.

Logic per scan:
- If NOT Mode: manual. Manual outputs from buttons with interlock. Clear auto state to WAIT_A, CompletionLight false.
- If Mode: auto.

Auto: outputs MotorForward, MotorReverse=false, CompletionLight computed.

Order of evaluation matters per tests. Let's look at T2 step 3: SensorA true, ButtonA true, phase WAIT_A → MotorForward true same scan. Yes transition affects same observed scan.

Step 4: no sensors, motor still forward (phase MOVE_AB).

Step 5: SensorB true, phase MOVE_AB → arrive → stop motor (MotorForward false), transition to WAIT_B same scan.

Step 6: SensorB true, ButtonB → MotorForward true (phase MOVE_BC).

Step 7: SensorC true, phase MOVE_BC → arrive → motor false, phase WAIT_C, light false.

Step 8: SensorC true, ButtonC → light true. Phase maybe WAIT_C still or DONE. Light on.

Step 9: SensorC true, no button → light stays true.

Step 10: SensorC false → light off.

P6: G(auto & removed -> !light) — removed = NOT SensorC. So in auto always when sensor C false, light off. But careful: if pre-phase WAIT_C and sensorC false, light off. Also light only true when in WAIT_C (or done) and sensorC true. Actually simplest: CompletionLight in auto = (phase = WAIT_C or DONE) AND SensorC AND previously triggered? Let's think: when arriving at C with SensorC true but ButtonC not yet pressed, light false. So need a flag: completed.

Let's define CompletionLight = autoComp AND SensorC. autoComp set when phase WAIT_C and SensorC and ButtonC. Cleared when SensorC false (removal). 

But P6 says G(auto & removed -> !light) — that's satisfied since light = comp AND SensorC.

But also once removed, comp should clear so if product returns... Better clear comp when NOT SensorC.

Test T3 step 1: Mode auto, SensorA false, ButtonB true, ButtonC true. Phase WAIT_A, no SensorA, so nothing. Motor false, light false. Fine.

T3 step2: SensorA true, ButtonA false, ButtonB true → WAIT_A requires ButtonA; ButtonB ignored. Motor false. Good.

Note "Buttons are level signals accepted only in their corresponding station wait. One phase transition is accepted per call."

Now arrival priority: In MOVE_AB, if SensorB → stop. Priority over anything.

Implementation order:

```
// defaults
MotorForward := FALSE;
MotorReverse := FALSE;

IF NOT Mode THEN
    // manual
    phase := WAIT_A;
    comp := FALSE;
    CompletionLight := FALSE;
    IF ForwardButton AND NOT ReverseButton THEN
        MotorForward := TRUE;
    ELSIF ReverseButton AND NOT ForwardButton THEN
        MotorReverse := TRUE;
    END_IF
ELSE
    // automatic
    CASE phase OF
    WAIT_A:
        IF SensorA AND ButtonA THEN
            phase := MOVE_AB;
            MotorForward := TRUE;
        END_IF
    MOVE_AB:
        IF SensorB THEN
            phase := WAIT_B;
            MotorForward := FALSE;
        ELSE
            MotorForward := TRUE;
        END_IF
    WAIT_B:
        IF SensorB AND ButtonB THEN
            phase := MOVE_BC;
            MotorForward := TRUE;
        END_IF
    MOVE_BC:
        IF SensorC THEN
            phase := WAIT_C;
            MotorForward := FALSE;
        ELSE
            MotorForward := TRUE;
        END_IF
    WAIT_C:
        IF SensorC AND ButtonC THEN
            comp := TRUE;
        END_IF
    END_CASE
    CompletionLight := comp AND SensorC;
END_IF
```

Wait, comp clearing: when SensorC false, light off. But comp retained true; if product comes back to C later, light might turn on without ButtonC. Let's clear comp when NOT SensorC. Add: IF NOT SensorC THEN comp := FALSE; END_IF. But careful in WAIT_C setting comp same scan: order. In WAIT_C with SensorC and ButtonC, SensorC true so no clear. Fine.

But also should clear comp when arriving at C? Scenario: one product only. Keep simple.

Actually issue: in MOVE_AB and MOVE_BC we set MotorForward := TRUE, but arrival check uses SensorB/SensorC. What if SensorB true while in WAIT_A? Should not happen much.

Also P4 arrival: in MOVE_AB SensorB true → fwd false. Handled.

Also phase transitions "one per call": in MOVE_AB with SensorB, goes WAIT_B but does not then process ButtonB same call. Good since CASE.

T2 step 3: phase WAIT_A, SensorA & ButtonA → MOVE_AB, MotorForward true. Good.

T2 step 1: phase WAIT_A init, no sensor → motor false. Good.

Now "Entering manual mode clears automatic state and completion; return to automatic waits for A." Handled.

Need retained phase variable declaration inside VAR (persistent across calls). In CODESYS FB, VAR variables are retained across calls automatically. Use VAR with enum.

Define DUT enum E_Phase : (WAIT_A, MOVE_AB, WAIT_B, MOVE_BC, WAIT_C). And internally comp BOOL.

Declaration:
```
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Task
VAR_INPUT
  Mode : BOOL;
  ...
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
  MotorForward : BOOL;
  MotorReverse : BOOL;
  CompletionLight : BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR
  phase : E_Phase := E_Phase.WAIT_A;
  comp : BOOL := FALSE;
END_VAR
```

supporting_objects: DUT E_Phase with kind DUT.

Let me write declaration carefully, no END_FUNCTION_BLOCK.

DUT declaration for enum: probably
name: E_Phase, kind: DUT, declaration: "TYPE E_Phase : (WAIT_A, MOVE_AB, WAIT_B, MOVE_BC, WAIT_C); END_TYPE"

Initial value with enum member prefix: `:= E_Phase.WAIT_A` — in some compilers, need `E_Phase.WAIT_A` which is fine in CODESYS. Could just use `WAIT_A`. Safer: phase : E_Phase := WAIT_A; Hmm CODESYS supports both. Use E_Phase.WAIT_A.

CASE phase OF E_Phase.WAIT_A: ... Use E_Phase.WAIT_A labels.

Let me submit.

MotorReverse := FALSE default. Interlock satisfied.

Let me build the JSON.
